feedback.problem: The points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(0,-7)$ and $(6,1)$, respectively, and the segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ is a diameter of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.
feedback.worked_solution:
The diameter can be calculated using the distance formula: 

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(0-6)}^{2}+{(-7-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+(-8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+64} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is half the diameter:

$$
r=\frac{d}{2}=\frac{10}{2}=5
$$
